description: SASRec predicts the next item using causal self-attention over a user's interaction history. Learned item and position embeddings feed attention and feed-forward blocks; the resulting sequence representation scores candidate items through embedding dot products. Attention selects relevant recent or distant interactions. Source: [Self-Attentive Sequential Recommendation](https://arxiv.org/html/1808.09781).
motivation: Balance the simplicity of short-range transition models with the ability to capture longer histories. The supplied task applies this established baseline to four Amazon datasets; it does not specify a new cold-start mechanism.
implementation_notes: Start from RecHarness sasrec_perdataset and preserve all four dataset routes. Use preprocessing seed 0, training seed 42, DATA_DIR=os.environ['GAGC_DATA_DIR'], and the effective 200-epoch default. Select using host-measured macro validation HR@10 under the pinned candidate protocol. Save artifacts beneath the trial directory and keep the predictor writer consistent with the trained architecture. Preserve DiagnosisProbe(view, device).run_full_diagnosis(train_loader), its metrics and metric_definitions, and the compatibility interface. Use only permitted public data, one GPU per trial, and the shared 43,200 GPU-second budget. No benchmark improvements have been demonstrated.
pseudocode:
for category in four_categories:
    load unchanged RecHarness splits with preprocessing_seed=0
    initialize category SASRec with training_seed=42
    for epoch in configured_epochs(default=200):
        for sequence, positive, negative in training_batches:
            features = causal_SASRec(sequence)
            loss = masked_sampled_binary_cross_entropy(features, positive, negative)
            update_parameters(loss)
    save_model_and_configuration_under_trial_directory()
write_predictor_with_matching_architecture_and_category_routing()
# Host independently measures macro validation HR@10.

originality.positive: Provides a clear application of selective attention to sequential recommendation.
originality.negative: SASRec is an established method, and the supplied description adds constraints rather than a novel algorithm.

future_potential.positive: Offers a useful baseline for controlled experiments with regularization, losses, sampling, and permitted metadata.
future_potential.negative: Item-ID embeddings alone offer limited support for unseen items; any cold-start extension requires separate validation.

code_difficulty.positive: The existing per-dataset SASRec baseline supplies most required components.
code_difficulty.negative: Architecture changes must remain consistent across training, predictor generation, dataset routing, and diagnosis probes.
